periods.public: Participants discuss the need for data on accessibility, funding stability, and historical precedents. They divide the available research topics to cover logistical, financial, and personnel constraints.

lines.Yumi: Suggests looking at how people reach the library.
lines.Benjamin: Suggests checking past attempts at similar services.
lines.Shion: Suggests checking staff skills and certifications.

lines.Yumi: Chooses bus links and winter road closures.
lines.Benjamin: Chooses two programmes begun six years ago and attendance sheets.
lines.Shion: Chooses volunteer register and neighbourhood associations.
lines.Minako: Chooses county grant terms and running and equipment lines.
lines.Daisuke: Chooses bus links and attendance sheets.

periods.public: Participants share their findings regarding budget gaps, transport failures, and the lack of qualified supervisors. They debate whether to prioritize reach or sustainability.

lines.Yumi: Reports on the loss of bus links and road closures.
lines.Benjamin: Reports on the failure of past digitisation and success of groups.
lines.Shion: Reports on the lack of certified supervisors for tools.
lines.Minako: Reports on the short-term nature of grants.
lines.Daisuke: Reports on high demand in outer wards.

lines.Shion: Questions who will manage technical equipment.
lines.Minako: Points out the risk of funding cliffs.
lines.Daisuke: Highlights the isolation of certain residents.

lines.Yumi: Asks if any option avoids road dependencies.
lines.Benjamin: Asks if any option has a proven long-term model.
lines.Shion: Asks if any option uses existing volunteers.
lines.Minako: Asks about the cost of vehicle maintenance.
lines.Daisuke: Asks if we can bring services to the people.

periods.public: The group evaluates the candidates against the discovered constraints. They weigh the trade-off between high demand in remote areas and the risks of vehicle costs and staffing.

lines.Yumi: Argues for the option that reaches the outer wards.
lines.Benjamin: Argues for the option that mirrors the successful six-year-old groups.
lines.Shion: Argues for the option that doesn't require certified tool supervisors.
lines.Minako: Argues for the option with the most stable funding path.
lines.Daisuke: Argues for the option that solves the transport gap.

lines.Yumi: Questions the cost of the vehicle option.
lines.Benjamin: Questions the feasibility of the digital portal given past failures.
lines.Shion: Questions the safety of the workshop without a technician.
lines.Minako: Notes that the vehicle line already overran last year.
lines.Daisuke: Notes that the outer wards have the highest need.

lines.Yumi: Considers the budget warning from Minako.
lines.Benjamin: Suggests the community-led model is the safest bet.
lines.Shion: Agrees that the community-led model avoids staffing gaps.
lines.Minako: Agrees that the community-led model is fiscally sustainable.
lines.Daisuke: Wonders if the community-led model can reach the outer wards.

lines.Yumi: Decides based on the balance of reach and risk.
lines.Benjamin: Casts vote based on historical evidence.
lines.Shion: Casts vote based on personnel availability.
lines.Minako: Casts vote based on budget longevity.
lines.Daisuke: Casts vote based on geographic equity.

seats.Minako: Focuses on the long-term shape of funding. She uses financial data to steer the group away from high-maintenance options.
seats.Yumi: Focuses on external factors like transport. She seeks a solution that remains functional despite environmental changes.
seats.Benjamin: Focuses on historical records. He uses past failures and successes to evaluate the viability of the proposals.
seats.Daisuke: Focuses on geographic accessibility. He advocates for those who cannot physically reach the main branch.
seats.Shion: Focuses on the internal skill set of the staff. He evaluates options based on whether the necessary expertise exists on the roster.
